questions.stem: A 22-year-old married woman has had severe, recurrent depression associated with multiple suicide attempts. She has been stabilized for the past 3 months on paroxetine and is now pregnant. Which of the following is the most appropriate management?

options.text: Discontinue paroxetine due to avoid prematurity
Continue paroxetine and monitor for depression
Discontinue paroxetine to avoid fetal damage

questions.stem: A 25-year-old woman in her first trimester of pregnancy has come for a routine prenatal visit. She used to smoke one pack of cigarettes per day, and is now being advised to quit smoking. Which of the following is the greatest risk to her unborn child?

A 28-year-old primigravida 8 weeks gestation woman attended her first antenatal appointment. During the history assessment, she reports that she never had chickenpox. A serum blood titer is drawn and is negative for antibodies. Which of the following is the next best step in management?

A gravida 2 para 0 woman presents to the Maternal Health Clinic reporting that she has not menstruated for the past 2 months. The previous pregnancy had resulted in a stillbirth at 34 weeks' gestation. A human chorionic gonadotropin test is now positive. She has been trying to conceive for the past 6 months. She is afraid of having another stillbirth and asks to be vaccinated against everything. Which of the following vaccines is most appropriate to administer?

A gravida 3, para 2 is 16 weeks' pregnant presents to the obstetrics Clinic concerned about an outbreak of illness in her child's school and the potential effects on the fetus. Which of the following vaccines is recommended at this time?
Which of the following vaccine is contraindicated during pregnancy?
Which of the following interventions is the best to use with pregnant women who smoke?

A 32-year-old multiparous woman is admitted for induction of labour at 41 weeks and 2 days gestation. She had prior 2 uneventful vaginal deliveries. A pelvic examination shows the cervix is dilated at 2 cm and is 50% effaced with a medium consistency and mid-anterior position. The presenting part is at -2 station. Which of the following methods would be most appropriate for labour induction?

A 29-year-old primigravida presented at 22 weeks of gestation with mild lower abdominal pain. Abdominal examination reveals that the uterus is corresponding to the gestational age with positive fetal heart. Vaginal examination reveals a short soft cervix, which is 1.5 cm dilated with herniation of fetal membranes. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
A patient is seen at 8 weeks' gestation in an Antenatal Clinic with a diagnosis of cervical incompetence. Which of the following is the most appropriate management?

options.text: Insertion cervical suture the same week
Confirm the diagnosis by Hegar dilator

questions.stem: A woman presents at her 9th week of pregnancy with severe vaginal bleeding, lower abdominal pain and passage of the fetus through the vagina. On vaginal examination, cervix is open and tissue seen in the cervix. Which of the following the most appropriate management?

options.text: Fluid replacement and evacuation and curettage.

questions.stem: A 23-year-old woman G3 P02002 at 20 weeks' gestation with history of previous 2 preterm deliveries attend Antenatal Clinic. Current pregnancy is uneventful. An ultrasound shows size corresponds to date, anterior placenta and cervical length is 30 mm. Which of the following is the most appropriate intervention?

A 21-year-old primigravida is being monitored in the Labor and Delivery Unit. She is currently at 37 weeks of gestation and the cardiotocogram is done. It is persistently showing the pattern for the last 90 minutes. Therefore, she is concerned about the reason of this pattern in the fetal monitoring (see image). Which of the following would best describe the cause of this pattern in response to the patients concern?

A 37-year-old woman G2 P1001 at 20 weeks' gestation presents for a routine prenatal visit. She has no complaints. Her previous pregnancy has been unremarkable. She has chronic hypertension and history of cholecystectomy. She admits to smoking cigarettes several packs a day for relaxation and says she has read several papers that show no increased risk of congenital anomalies. Doppler shows fetal heart rate at 156 beat per minute. Blood pressure 108/68 mmHg Heart rate 100 /min Respiratory rate 16 /min Temperature 36.6 °C Oxygen saturation 95 % Which of the following is the best course of action?

options.text: Schedule her in 4-week time in antenatal clinic
Refer her to a social worker for possible substance abuse
Educate her about the possibility of delivering a small infant

questions.stem: A 30-year-old woman gravida 4, para 3 woman presents to the Antenatal Clinic at 32 weeks' gestation with headache and swelling of the feet. At the initial antenatal visit, there was +2 pitting edema of the lower extremities and the face appears swollen. Dipstick of the urine shows proteinuria. The fundal height is 28 cm and the fetal heart rate was 140-150 beats per minute with good variability. She reports regular fetal movements. Blood pressure 150/100 mmH Heart rate 90 /min Respiratory rate 26 /min Temperature 37.1° C Which additional clinical findings would be associated with intrauterine growth restriction?

options.text: The presence of a low lying placenta
History of smoking 10 cigarettes per day

options.text: Admit the patient to the ward

Fetal heart baseline 160 bpm with minimal variability and repetitive late deceleration (see lab results). Blood pressure 170/100 mmHg Heart rate 120 /min Temperature 37.7 °C Hb 75 130-170 g/L (Male) 120-160 g/L (Female) Platelets count 110 150-400 x 109/L Fibrinogen 2.5 2-4 g/L Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 34-week pregnant woman presents in labor with contractions occurring every 4 minutes, she also has vaginal bleeding which is heavier than normal menstrual flow. The fetus is in a back- down position, transverse lie, and the cervix is dilated 3 cm with bulging membranes. The fetal heart rate is 170 bpm. The sonography showed a posterior fundal placenta with a retroplacental sonolucent area. Which of the following is the most appropriate initial management?

A 25-year-old primigravida at 38 weeks of gestation is being monitored in the Labor and Delivery Ward. Abdominal examination reveals an average size fetus of 3 kg in cephalic presentation and well engaged head. Cervical examination shows 5 cm dilated, 70% effaced and -3 station for the last 4 hours. She is not distressed and not on epidural analgesia. Fetal monitoring is done (see image). Which of the following is the best next step of management?

A 35-year-old woman G5 P4004 in labor and has been fully dilated for the last 2 hours. Maternal exhaustion is noted after pushing efforts for the last hour. She is not on epidural analgesia and the cardiotocogram shows category 1. Abdominal examination shows an average size fetus of 2.7 kg, cephalic presentation with 4/5 palpable head. On pelvic examination, the cervix is fully dilated and 100% effaced with -3 station. Which of the following is the best next step?

A 38-year-old woman G5 P4004 at 39 weeks of gestation is in labor room and on epidural analgesia. She has been fully dilated for the last 30 minutes and all of sudden, the uterine contractions cease despite of oxytocin infusion along with fetal deceleration and mild vaginal bleeding. Which of the following is the best next step?

options.text: Stop oxytocin infusion and perform an immediate cesarean section
Left lateral position and review in 20 minutes
Stop the epidural analgesia infusion pump

questions.stem: A 39-year-old woman G2 P1001 at 37 weeks of gestation presented in labor. She has history of cesarean section due to breech presentation 2 years ago. It has been 2 hours since she was declared fully dilated and current pelvic examination reveals 10-cm dilatation, fully effacement and +3 to +4 station. She is contracting 4 strong contractions in 10 minutes. The cardiotocogram is showing occasional early deceleration. Which of the following in the best next step?

A 40-year-old woman at 37 weeks of gestation with polyhydramnios presented in active labor following spontaneous rupture of membranes. Cardiotocogram shows persistent fetal bradycardia. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 26-year-old woman G2 P1001 admitted to the hospital in active labor and ruptured membranes at 38 weeks of gestation. Upon vaginal examination, the cervix was 6 cm dilated and 1 cm long. The orbital ridge and orbits, saddle of the nose, mouth, and chin were palpable. What is the scientific term for this fetal presentation?

A primigravida at 37 weeks gestation known to have bicornuate uterus complains of subcostal discomfort and fetal kicking is appreciated in the lower abdomen mainly. Leopold maneuver; shows global soft presenting part with sluggish ballottement by first and second pelvic grips. Fetal heart detected at the level of maternal umbilicus. Which of the following is the most likely fetal presentation?

What is the recommended method of delivery if this fetal presentation persisted?

A 27-year-old primigravida at 39 weeks' gestation presents to the hospital complaining of spontaneous watery gush. A speculum examination is performed and small amount of fluid is seen in the vault. Nitazine paper test indicates a pH of 7. Which of the following is another reliable test to confirm amniotic fluid leaks?

options.text: Indigo carmine injection into the amniotic sac
Methylene blue injection into the amniotic sac
Ultrasonography to assess amniotic fluid volume
Microscopy to detect arborization or ferning of fluid

An hour later the obstetrician noticed a loop of the umbilical cord below the fetal head. Foetal Heart Rate 120 beat/min. Which of the following is the most appropriate immediate management?

A fetal monitoring strip showed 2 contractions in 10 minutes with a reassured non-stress test. Which of the following is the most appropriate management?

The cervix was 6 cm dilated, 80% effaced. Mouth, lips, nose and orbital hollows were palpable. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step in management?

A 30-year-old woman is in the second stage of labour for 3 hours by now. She is not on epidural analgesia. Abdominal examination shows an average size fetus of about 3 kg, in cephalic presentation with only 1/5 palpable head abdominally. Pelvic examination confirms that her cervix is fully dilated, fully effaced at +2 station. Which of the following is the most appropriate action at this point?

A 32-year-old pregnant patient at 36 weeks is in active labor and complaining of abdominal pain that has been increasing in intensity and continuous. She denies any bleeding. Abdominal examination reveals a 38 cm fundal height, and the uterus is found to be tender and tense. Pelvic examination reveals a 6 cm dilated cervix. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step in management?

A 30-year-old G3 P2002 patient at 38 weeks of gestation in the Labor Room is in active labor, the patient is free of pain after initiation of epidural analgesia. She was diagnosed with pre- eclampsia with severe features and was started on MgSO4. On examination, the abdomen is showing a cephalic term pregnancy with 2/5 palpable head. On pelvic examination, the cervix is 6 cm dilated and fully effaced at - 1 station. The patient is on oxytocin infusion and is contracting regularly. The cardiotocogram is done (see image). Which of the following is most possible cause of cardiotogram findings?

A 30-year-old G3 P2002 patient at 38 weeks of gestation is in active labor, she is free of pain after initiation of epidural analgesia. She was diagnosed with severe features of pre-eclampsia and was started on MgSO4. On examination, the abdomen is showing a cephalic term pregnancy with 2/5 palpable head. On pelvic examination, the cervix is 6 cm dilated and fully effaced. The patient is on oxytocin infusion and is contracting regularly. The cardiotocogram is done (see image). Blood pressure 90/50 mmHg Heart rate 76 /min Temperature 36.6 °C Which of the following is most possible cause of cardiotogram findings?

A 30-year-old woman G3 P2002 at 38 weeks of gestation is in the Labor Room. Changes on the cardiotocogram is noted while she is on oxytocin infusion with regular contractions. The diagnosis of pre- eclampsia with severe features was entertained earlier on and started her on MgSO4 accordingly. The labor pain is well-controlled after initiation of epidural analgesia. On examination, the abdomen is showing a cephalic term pregnancy with 0/5 palpable head. Pelvic examination shows cervix is 6 cm dilated and fully effaced and presenting part is at +1 station (see image). Which of the following would explain the cause of the cardiotocogram findings?

A 22-year-old primigravida woman at 38 weeks gestation is in active labor for 4 hours. Cervical dilatation is 5 cm, +1 station. Examination 5 hours later demonstrates no change compared to the previous findings. Contractions occur every 3 minutes and lasts 60 seconds. Fetal hear rate is of category 1 cardiotocograph. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step?
Which of the following positions of a patient in labour would most likely result in the development of a third or fourth-degree laceration?

A 30-year-old woman G4 P3003 at 34 weeks of pregnancy with breech presentation is asking about the possibility of external cephalic version, after reviewing the patient's information. Her first delivery was a caesarean section and was followed by a spontaneous vaginal delivery 4 years ago; she has no other significant medical or surgical history. The ultrasound is showing a single viable fetus of 3.2 kg with an anterior low-lying placenta and an amniotic fluid index of 4 cm. On examination, the patient is found to be in early labor and the pelvic assessment reveals a 3 cm dilated cervix with an intact membrane. Cardiotocography is done (see image). Which of the following indicates the absolute contraindication for external cephalic version?

A 27-year-old woman primigravida at 39 weeks' gestation has been laboring for a few hours. Her cervix is 6 cm dilated, 80% effaced, and fetal vertex is at 0 station. Membranes have been ruptured for 20 hours and her labor is being augmented with oxytocin. Non-stress test is done (see image). Blood pressure 110/76 mmHg Heart rate 82 /min Respiratory rate 18 /min Temperature 37.2 °C Oxygen saturation 95 % Which of the following is the most appropriate in management?

A 30-year-old woman G2 P2002 at 32 weeks' gestation presents to Emergency Department complaining of lower abdominal and back pain, which has increased in frequency and intensity over the last few hours. Abdominal examination shows fundal height equals to 32 cm, longitudinal lie fetus and cephalic presentation. Fetal heart was positive and cardiotocography is reactive with 2-3 uterine contractions per 10 minutes. Vaginal examination shows 1 cm dilated cervix, 70% effacement, -3 station and cephalic. Which of the following is the most appropriate step in management?

options.text: Inform neonatologist, administer corticosteroids and strict bed rest.
Inform neonatologist, administer corticosteroids and hydrate the patient.
Inform neonatologist, administer tocolylics and start intravenous antibiotics.
Inform neonatologist, administer intravenous antibiotics and strict bed rest.

questions.stem: A 19-year-old woman presented with crampy, lower abdominal pain beginning with the onset of menses every month, and lasting for 2 to 3 days. There was no pain between menses, but reported radiation of pain to the lower back and upper thighs, along with nausea, fatigue, and headache which has been present for several years and progressively getting worse. Physical examination normal. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 28-year-old woman at 24 weeks' gestation presented to the clinic for a routine examination. A pelvic examination showed a watery grey-colored discharge, fish-like smell. There were no signs of inflammation of the vagina or cervix. She reported some itching and moderate discomfort. The vaginal pH 5.1. A sample of the vaginal discharge was collected for analysis. Which of the following is the most likely finding?

A 25-year-old woman presented to the clinic with an unpleasant-smelling discharge. A speculum examination showed vaginal discharge, grey-green in color. The cervix was covered with papillae with light-red color. A specimen of vaginal secretions was obtained for a wet-prep microscopy which showed unicellular organisms with flagella. Which of the following is the most appropriate management?

A 26-year-old nulliparous patient presented to the clinic with vaginal itching and increased vaginal discharge. She had been diagnosed with a positive pregnancy test 3 months ago. A pelvic examination showed a yellow-white discharge at the vaginal introitus. The labia were inflamed and covered with scratch marks. The vaginal discharge was fishy smell pH 4.8. Which of the following is the most appropriate treatment?

A 23-year-old woman presented with vaginal discharge with an unpleasant smell. Examination confirmed a homogenous greyish-white vaginal discharge that has a high PH. A saline wet- preparation examination of the discharge showed "clue cells* and with application of potassium hydroxide a fishy smell was generated. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 21-year-old woman presented with an abnormal vaginal discharge, burning on micturition, and blood spotting for the past 2 months. On genital examination, there was an eroded and friable (strawberry appearance) cervix, with a yellow-green mucopurulent discharge (see report). Lab Testing: >10 PMNs per oil immersion field. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 22-year-old diabetic woman presented with vaginal discharge and pruritus. The discharge is thick, grey and odorless. On physical examination, her vulva was erythematous and swollen. The vagina has a white-grey discharge that is adherent to the mucosa. Microscopic examination of the discharge confirmed the presence of spores. Which of the following is the most likely pathogen?

A 27-year-old woman presented with vaginal itching and an unpleasant smelling discharge. Itching gets worse at night and after intercourse. Physical examination confirmed a frothy and yellow-green vaginal discharge. Her vulva is erythematous and edematous and the cervix is inflamed and friable (see report). Wet Preparation: Flagellated protozoa. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 35-year-old woman attended the Gynecological Clinic complaining of greenish-yellow purulent vaginal discharge that has started after her period. Upon vaginal examination, there was multifocal rounded macular erythematous lesions (like a spotted rash or bruise), and there was pelvic tenderness. Which of the following conditions is the most likely diagnosis?

A 29-year-old woman complaining of a heavy vaginal discharge for the past 2 weeks. The discharge was thin and a greyish white color with a slight fishy vaginal odor. On examination, a copious, thin, whitish discharge is seen adherent to the vaginal wall. Vaginal pH 5.5 Which of the following is the most appropriate treatment?

A 33-year-old woman comes to the clinic complaining of recent onset of vaginal itching. Physical examination of the vagina revealed a thick, odorless white cottage cheese-like vaginal discharge that adheres to the mucosa. She has recently finished a course of antibiotics for an upper respiratory tract infection. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 48-year-old woman patient suffers from several episodes of vaginal discharge and itching around the genital area. The discharge is white and curd-like. The patient's spouse does not have any related condition. Microscopy of the discharge revealed budding yeast and pseudohyphae. The patient's symptoms might be associated with which of the following conditions?

A 21-year-old woman patient complained of severe vulvovaginal itching and discharge. There are no urinary or other symptoms, and annual papanicolaou tests have all been normal. On inspection, Vulvar erythema with swelling. Speculum examination revealed a thick, white, curdy discharge adherent to the vaginal walls with no dour. A gross and microscopic examination of the vaginal discharge was done; the wet mount revealed no evidence of clue cells or trichomonads and the KOH prepped slide confirmed several pseudohyphae (see lab results). pH 4.0 3.8-4.5 Whiff test negative negative Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 28-year-old woman presented with a history of a copious white vaginal discharge associated with intense vulvar irritation and itching for four days. Microscopic examination revealed evidence of pseudohyphae. Which of the following is the most appropriate treatment?

A 24-year-old woman came to the clinic complaining of yellowish offensive vaginal discharge and itching for 2 weeks. She has no other significant medical history. Vaginal swab done which showed motile flagellated organisms on wet film microscopy. Which of the following is the best treatment option?

A 24-year-old married woman came to the clinic complaining of yellowish offensive vaginal discharge and itching for 2 weeks. She has no other significant medical history. Vaginal swab done which showed motile flagellated organisms on wet film microscopy. Appropriate treatment was initiated. Which of the following is the best management option for her husband?

A 34-year-old woman presented with profuse milky vaginal discharge. Office diagnosis demonstrates fishy odor (positive Whiff test). A wet-mount preparation of the discharge (see image). Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 30-year-old woman is complaining of a newly developed red and painful swelling on the vulva. On examination, the appearance of a solitary lesion is noticed, located at the 5 o'clock position on the vestibule. It is red, tender, fluid-filled and appears to be infected. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 30-year-old woman comes to the clinic with anogenital lesions that appear as sharply marginalized. They are smooth, flat-topped, 1 to 2 cm in diameter, moist papules and small plaques. The patient admits of having multiple sexual partners and of use of illicit drugs (see image). Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 32-year-old woman presents with a smelly vaginal discharge associated with intense itching. Her husband has a history of slight urethral discharge. A pelvic examination confirmed strawberry spots on the cervix. Which one of the following is the most appropriate treatment?

A 26-years-old woman presents with vaginal discharge that is characterized by a thin milky appearance with a fish-like odor. On examination, the vaginal pH of 4.5 was found. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 35-year-old woman G4 P2012 at 26 weeks' gestation, presented for a 50-gram oral glucose tolerance test. 1 hour later by finger stick sample glucose was 8.1 mmol/L. Which vaginal infection is she at the highest risk of contracting?

A 25-year-old woman had a severe pelvic inflammatory disease 2 years ago that was treated by intravenous antibiotics. The isolated organism was chlamydia trachomatis. Since then the woman was trying for pregnancy and failed to conceive. She had a normal regular period and her husband had a normal seminal analysis. Hysterosalpingogram revealed normal uterine cavity and no free spillage of the injected dye bilaterally (see lab results). Body mass index 35 kg/m2 Follicle-stimulating hormone 4.5 5-20 IU/L Luteinizing hormone 3.9 5-22 U/L Which of the following is the most appropriate method of management?

options.text: Induction of ovulation followed by normal intercourse
Induction of ovulation followed by intrauterine insemination
Weight reduction to reach body mass index of 23 kg/m2

The patient's history reveals that she became pregnant while using an intrauterine contraceptive device 4 years ago and in her second pregnancy; she underwent a cesarean section, which was complicated by postpartum endometritis. Her menstrual cycles have been irregular for the last 4 months with heavier flow than usual. Which of the following is an absolute contraindication to the insertion of an intrauterine contraceptive device?

A 30-year-old woman is undergoing a laparotomy for ovarian cystectomy. She is a known smoker and she is on oral combined contraceptive pills for the last 6 years. During surgery, she developed tachycardia, hypoxemia and hypotension. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 33-year-old woman presents with a history of amenorrhea for a year following dilatation and curettage because of abnormal uterine bleeding. She underwent both progesterone and combined estrogen and progesterone withdrawal tests with no response. Her serum FSH level was normal, Which of the following syndromes is the most likely diagnosis?

A 48-year-old woman has had 2 inflammatory pap smears 3 months apart and a normal pelvic examination. A colposcopically directed biopsy of a normal appearing cervix revealed invasive carcinoma. Which of the following is the best next step in management?

A 22-year-old woman presents to the Women's Health Clinic for a routine examination. Her menstrual cycle occurs every 28 days and lasts for 5 days with moderate bleeding. Clinical breast examination showed bilateral symmetry with no abnormal findings on palpation. However, she reported regular breast tenderness that began 3 days prior to menses. There was no known maternal or paternal history of cancer. She wishes to become pregnant within the next 2 years. Which of the following screening tests should be done?

A 60-year-old woman's recent pap smear yielded a result of Atypical squamous cells of undetermined significance (ASC-US). She was given topical vaginal estrogen for one month and was scheduled for another pap smear a week after the treatment cycle has completed. The second pap smear showed ASC-US as well. Which of the following is the most appropriate next investigation?

A 34-year-old woman non-smoker with 2 previous normal deliveries presented for a routine pap smear and her last pap was normal 7 years ago. The patient has had 1 episode of venereal warts at 18 year-old with no recurrence. The rest of her history is not significant (see report). Pap smear: A typical squamous cells of undetermined significance. What will be the first step in management?

A 30-year-old married woman has had an abnormal Papanicolaou test result. Repeated smears were suggestive of high-grade intrepithelial lesions. Pelvic and rectal examinations were normal. Which of the following is the next step in management?

A 30-year-old para 3 woman presented with a significant history of smoking 2 packs of per week for the past 7 years. She was using a progestin-only pills. She has had annual Papanicolaou examinations for the past 9 years and all results have been normal. Bimanual pelvic examination showed normal findings. Papinicolaou smear repeated with results of low-grade epithelial lesions. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step in management?

A 40-year-old sexually active patient presents for cervical cancer screening. Physical examination is unremarkable, menstruation is regular with a 28-day cycle and last menstrual period was 5 days ago. Which of the following is the best advice about Pap smear?

options.text: Three negative results and no further screening

questions.stem: A 58-year-old woman presented with postmenopausal bleeding. Pelvic examination revealed a fungating irregular mass from the cervix. Which of the following has the highest diagnostic value?

A 33-year-old woman presents to the clinic after an incidental finding of a mass in the cervix. She denies any complaints of pelvic pressure, pain or menorrhagia but admits to have occasional post coital bleeding (see image). Which of the following is the most appropriate in counselling the patient?

options.text: Excision to be performed in the clinic
Admission and further workup is required
Reassurance and follow-up in a few months
Broad spectrum antibiotics need to be started

questions.stem: A 40-year-old woman complains of Post-coital bleeding. Speculum examination reveals cervical mass. Which of the following is the most appropriate next investigation?

A 35-year-old healthy woman attended the Gynecological Clinic for her regular Pap smear screening. Upon speculum pelvic examination, the uterine cervix appeared raised irregular mass measuring 10 X 12 mm localized on the cervix left lateral aspect.Which of the following is the most appropriate next step?

options.text: Reassurance until the pap smear result

questions.stem: A 38-year-old woman attended Outpatient Clinic complaining of fresh vaginal bleeding occurring after each intercourse. This problem has been disturbing her over the last 3 months. Upon examination, her speculum examination revealed normal cervix. The report of Pap smear is showing squamous cell carcinoma. Which of the following is the most appropriate next immediate action?

A 31-year-old woman P2 presented to the Women's Health Clinic for a routine physical examination. She has presented to routine health examinations annually for the last 5 years. Records indicate that in the previous year, she has negative tests for both the human papilloma virus and the papanicolaou cervical smear. This year both tests are with no abnormal findings. When should the tests be repeated?

A 35-year-old pregnant woman at 13-weeks of pregnancy presented with painless vaginal bleeding. Vaginal examination shows a suspicious lesion of the cervix (see report). Fetal ultrasound: Shows normal viable fetus and size corresponds to her gestational age. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step?
A 27-year-old sexually active woman came for annual examination. 3 years ago, she had a pap smear which was reported to be normal. Which of the following is the most appropriate management?
A 24-year-old woman comes to the clinic. She is married for 3 years and has no previous pap smears. She asks for a pap smear during the visit. Which of the following is the most appropriate action?

options.text: Should get pap smear during this visit
Do not screen now, wait until she is 30 years of age
Next screening after 5 years with a combination of cytology and HPV testing
Cervical cancer screening in women younger than 30 years is likely to lead to more harms than benefits

questions.stem: What is the recommended age to start Pap smear screening for cervical cancer in married women? A. 20-24
Which of the following is the recommended frequency of Pap smear screening for cervical cancer? A. Every year

A 55-year-old woman comes to the Gynecology Clinic complaining of a mass protruding through her vagina when standing for quite sometimes especially during cough and straining She has 7 children that were delivered vaginally. The last delivery was complicated by prolonged second stage and ended up with vacuum extraction delivery of a 4.2 Kg baby. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step?

A 67-year-old woman attended the Gynecological Clinic for the follow up of lichen sclerosus diagnosed a few years earlier. Upon examination, a small mass measuring 0.5 x 0.5 cm was identified on her right labia majora. Punch biopsy was taken from the lesion and sent for histopathology. Which of the following is the most likely histopathological finding?

A 57-year-old menopausal woman, presents for evaluation of post-menopausal bleeding. She is morbidly obese, hypertensive and diabetic. Endometrial sampling showed complex endometrial hyperplasia with atypia. Which of the following is the most appropriate treatment?

A 43-year-old woman gravida 2 para 2 has had oligoovulation due to polycystic ovary syndrome and used cyclic progesterone for withdrawal bleeding. Approximately 5 years ago, she discontinued taking progesterone. Which of the following risks is increased?

A 32-year-old obese woman with history of irregular menstruation and chronic anovulation, found to have atypical complex hyperplasia on endometrial biopsy. Which of the following is the most definitive treatment?

A 40-year-old woman is complaining of abnormal uterine bleeding. She is known diabetic on oral hypoglycemic agent for 5 years and her menarche at the age of 13. The last 3 cycles were heavy, however, denies any weight loss or palpitation. Which of the following would make the highest risk of endometrial cancer?

A 43-year-old never married woman is complaining of abnormal uterine bleeding for the last 3 months. She was placed on progestin tablets to control her bleeding by a family physician prior to referral. One of the sisters had a diagnosis of thyroid cancer 2 years ago. Blood pressure 110/70 mmHg Heart rate 76 /min Respiratory rate 16 /min BMI 17 kg/m2 Which of the following would make the highest risk of endometrial cancer?

A 62-year-old patient presented with vaginal bleeding. Investigations revealed a malignant tumor of uterine fundus. Which of the following groups of lymph nodes is likely affected in this condition and to be dissected during surgery?

A 57-year-old menopausal woman, presents for evaluation of postmenopausal bleeding. She is morbidly obese, hypertensive and diabetic. Endometrial sampling showed complex endometrial hyperplasia with atypia. Which of the following is the most appropriate treatment?

A 50-year-old P2+3 patient known to be diabetic and hypertensive, presented to the clinic complaining of abnormal uterine bleeding for the last 8 months, the menstrual period is regular every 30 days and lasts for 5 days, associated with blood clots and pain that is not relieved by simple analgesia. The patient had previously undergone myomectomy 12 years back and was known to have all her pregnancies induced as she had poly-cystic ovarian syndrome. On examination, the uterus was not palpable but on pelvic examination revealed a normal sized uterus and a healthy looking cervix with no adnexal mass. BMI 40 kg/m2 Which of the following is the most likely explanation for this patient's presentation?

A 60-year-old P5+3 patient is known to be diabetic and hypertensive presented to the clinic complaining of post-menopausal bleeding for the last 8 months. The patient had previously undergone myomectomy 12 years back and 3 surgical evacuation for incomplete miscarriage. On examination, the uterus was not palpable but on pelvic examination the uterus was found to be bulky and tender with no adnexal mass (see image). BMI 42 kg/m2 Which of the following is the most likely explanation for this patient's presentation?

A 60-year-old patient presents with postmenopausal bleeding for the last 8 months. The ultrasound is ordered (see image). Which of the following is the most appropriate next step in assessing this patient?

A 47-year-old woman, poorly controlled diabetic, complains of polymenorrhagia every couple of weeks. Body mass index 37 kg/m2 Which of the following is most appropriate investigation to establish the diagnosis?

options.text: Magnetic resonance imaging of the pelvis.

questions.stem: A 38-year-old woman presented with dysuria and increased frequency of urination. History reveals, she is allergic to sulfa, penicillin, and shellfish (see report). Blood Pressure 120/80 mmHg, Heart Rate 80 /min, Respiratory Rate 16 /min, Temperature 38.0° C Urine Dipstick: Positive for leukocyte esterase. Which of the following is the most appropriate treatment?

A patient comes for a follow-up 2 weeks after a vaginal hysterectomy with anterior and posterior repair; the patient had leakage of urine from the vagina during micturition. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 55-year-old woman presented to the clinic with urinary leakage for the last 6 weeks. She cannot hold her urine and urine leaks even before she reaches the bathroom. History revealed she has been menopause for the last 6 years. Which of the following is the first step in the evaluation?

A 58-year-old multiparous woman is complaining of urine leakage at laugh or cough. She is not able to hold her urine along with feeling of "dragging" or "balloon-like" sensation in the genital area for the past 4 months. Physical examination is normal except for bulging of the lower anterior vaginal wall. Which of the following is the most likely cause of those symptoms?

A 23-year-old pregnant woman presented with frequency and dysuria for 5 days (see lab result), Blood pressure 110/70 mmHg, Heart rate 76 /min, Temperature 37.6 °C Leukocytes 30 (0-3 per high power field) Which of the following is the best treatment option?

A 42-year-old P6036 complaining of vaginal fullness, heaviness and discomfort that progress over the day and becomes noticeable after prolonged standing. She used to apply manual pressure to empty her urinary bladder completely. She also had stress urinary incontinence. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 66-years-old woman presents with a single and asymptomatic bright-red papule at the urethral meatus. The surface bleeds easily on touch (see image). Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 56-year-old multiparous patient on oral estrogen, complains of painless urine incontinence when coughing, sneezing, or laughing for 1 year. On examination, there was mild vaginal atrophy and constrictor muscle laxity. Urinary incontinence is demonstrated in the lithotomy position with Valsalva maneuver (see report). Urinalysis: Normal. Which of the following would be the recommended management?

A 70-year-old man presents with urinary incontinence. The patient's bladder is palpably distended after voiding. The patient stated that he voids frequently, although he has difficulty initiating the urine stream.Which of the following is the most likely type of incontinence?

A 35-year-old woman delivered her fifth baby by vacuum extraction due to prolonged second stage of labor 3 months ago. The woman was complaining of leakage of urine when she coughed, sneezed or laughed. The symptoms have started after delivery and persisted since then Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
A 6-year-old girl brought by her mother with vulvar itching and bloody vaginal discharge for few days. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 55-year-old menopausal woman presented with vulvar irritation associated with urgency and frequency. Examination of the external genitalia revealed odorless watery discharge and generalized vulvar erythema with excoriation. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
A 22-year-old woman presented with headache, malaise and fever. Examination revealed multiple, bilateral painful anogenital vesicles. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
A 32-year-old pregnant woman at 26-weeks of gestation diagnosed with large genital warts in the vulva. Which of the following is the most appropriate management?
A 34-year-old patient at 38-weeks of pregnancy with genital chlamydia trachomatis. Which of the following is most commonly acquired infection by the newborn in such a condition?
A 27-year-old woman presented at 24-weeks of gestation with dysuria and lower abdominal pain. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step in management?

A 40-year-old P6 patient attends to the clinic complaining of dribbling of a small amount of urine with associated dyspareunia and dysuria. She denies any history of previous surgeries or the development of fever. Which of the following is the most likely cause of the symptoms?

A 40-year-old patient who is known to have COPD comes to the clinic complaining of small amounts of urine leaking every time she coughs; the patient denies having to wake up at night to pass urine and does not have dysuria or dyspareunia. BMI 40 kg/m2 Which of the following is the most probable cause?

A 50-year-old patient presents to the clinic complaining of urinary leaking on coughing and straining. She is not known to have any medical or previous surgical history. On examination. the abdomen is soft and is non-tender. Pelvic examination reveals a normal sized anteverted, non-tender uterus. There was mild amounts of urine leakage when the patient was asked to cough. Which of the following is the most appropriate management?

A 35-year-old woman delivered her first baby by vacuum extraction due to prolonged second stage of labor 3 months ago. The woman was complaining of leakage of urine when she coughed, sneezed or laughed. The symptoms have started since delivery and persisted since then. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
A 35-year-old nulliparous on treatment for hyperprolactinemia for the past year. When would pituitary imaging be indicated?

options.text: Prolactin level is twice the normal

questions.stem: A 25-year-old woman is 10 days postpartum and breastfeeding on demand. For 48 hours before presentation to the clinic, she has had episodes of chills with feeling weak and tired. Physical examination revealed redness of the left breast, and tenderness and excoriation of the areola. A left breast tender, mobile 3 cm dominant lump was found in the upper outer quadrant on palpation and left axillary lymphadenopathy was present (see lab results). Blood pressure 110/70 mmH, Heart rate 115 /min, Respiratory rate 20/min, Temperature 39.0° C Test Result Normal Values Hb 115 120-160 g/L WBC 14 4.5-10.5 x 109/L Neutrophils 80 40-60% Band cells 7 3-5% Basophils 1 0.5-1 % Eosinophils 1 1-4 % Lymphocytes 50 20-40 % Monocytes 2 2-8 % Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 25-year-old woman complained of swelling on one side of the labia. The swelling was first noticed 24 hours ago and has not improved despite warm tub soaking. There was a non-tender 3 cm slightly mobile cystic mass at approximately 7 o'clock on the right side of the vaginal introitus. Blood pressure 110/70 mmH, Heart rate 76 /min, Respiratory rate 18 /min, Temperature 37° C Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 56-year-old postmenopausal woman presents with a 1-year history of recurrent irritation in the pubic area. The patient reported itchiness with blood-stained discharge at times. The patient has tried a metronidazole suppositories as well as topical cream over the labia with little relief. Recently. the patient feels a pea-sized lump on the labia. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 68-year-old woman underwent a total abdominal hysterectomy and bilateral salpingo- oophorectomy. 3 days following the surgery, urinary catheter was removed and she was able to independently void 1 hour with an output of 35 ml/hr. She has been receiving fluids by continuous intravenous drip. She described the incisional pain as uncomfortable and rates it at a level 5 on the pain assessment scale. For pain relief, she was taking Ibuprofen 800 milligrams every 6 hours. The doctor considered her ready for discharge (see lab results). Blood pressure 118/68 mmHg, Heart rate 70 /min, Respiratory rate 20 /min, Temperature 37.4° C oral НСТ 0.37 0.37-0.48 Hb 122 120-160 g/L Which of the following would be a reason for this patient to remain in hospital?
What is the most common type of vulvar neoplasms?

A 45-year-old woman presented with itching of the vulva. On careful inspection in a bright light, an elevated localized watery red lesion measuring 0.5 cm was seen. She is diagnosed with vulvar intraepithelial neoplasia with carcinoma in situ. Which of the following is the best management?
Which of the following estrogen is the most abundant in human pregnancy?

An 18-year-old girl is complaining of the appearance of lesions that are firm, smooth and skin- colored. They located at the anogenital area and mons pubis. Occasionally they get inflamed and become red and are described to be of 2 to 3 mm in diameter with occasional itching (see image). Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 70-year-old comes to the clinic complaining of a slowly enlarging lesion at the labia majora, which does not heal and bleeds when traumatized (see image). Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 35-year-old obese woman notices soft, skin-colored, brown papules with short, thin stalks that are 1 to 3 mm developing on the multiple areas of the inguinal folds. She states that when they are traumatized, they become blue and purpuric (see image). Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A couple suffering from infertility asked the feto-maternal consultant about surrogacy as an option to treat their infertility. The hospital does not offer the service and the consultant is not sure if surrogacy is legal in Saudi Arabia. Which of the following is the most appropriate action?

options.text: Inform the couple that hospital doesn't provide the service
Warn the couple that surrogacy might be illegal in Saudi Arabia
Refer them to a colleague who has connections with surrogacy canters
Give them appointment after few weeks to have enough time to review the topic

questions.stem: A 23-year-old nulliparous woman with a history of infertility 2 years. Her menstrual cycle is regularly coming every 29 days. Which of the following is best used to confirm ovulation?

A 33-year-old woman delivered vaginally with right mediolateral episiotomy. An hour later, she was found to have an expanding 7 x 5 cm bluish, tense, and painful swelling of the perineum. Which of the following is the best management?

A 30-year-old woman gravida 4, para 3 woman presents to Antenatal Clinic at 32 weeks' gestation with headache and swelling of the feet. At the initial antenatal visit, there was +2 pitting edema of the lower extremities and the face appears swollen. Dipstick of the urine shows proteinuria. The fundal height is 28 cm and fetal heart rate was 140-150 beats per minute with good variability. She reports regular fetal movements. Blood pressure 150/100 mmg, Heart rate 90 /min, Respiratory rate 26 /min, Temperature 37.1° C Which additional clinical finding would be associated with intrauterine growth restriction?
A 34-year-old multiparous woman presents at 37 weeks' twins gestation with regular contractions. Which of the following fetal presentations is favourable for vaginal delivery?
A 2-day-old baby seen in clinic with mother for counseling about breastfeeding. Which of the following indicates adequate breastfeeding in a baby?
A 20-day-old premature baby brought to the clinic with the mother for counselling about breast feeding. Which of the following is low in mother's milk after premature delivery?
A 53-year-old woman has missed her period over the last 12 months. Which of the following hormones is likely to be altered as a result of the condition?

A 43-year-old woman G9 P5126 breastfeeding of her 5-month-old daughter comes to the clinic because of positive home pregnancy test. She does not know her last menstrual period. Which of the following would be the most useful method to determine her estimated date of delivery?

options.text: Transvaginal ultrasound as early as possible in the first trimester

questions.stem: A 40-year-old woman presents to the clinic complaining of heavy bleeding for the last 4-months. After taking a detailed history and full physical examination, the patient and her gynecologist reach a plan of management and decide to undergo a hysteroscopy. Which of the following is the most common complication of hysteroscopy?
A 22-year-old woman is seen in the Preconception Clinic. She is planning to get pregnant during winter season. Which of the following vaccine is recommended during preconception period?
A 26-year-old woman is seen in the preconception clinic for a routine visit. Which of the following is recommended during preconception period?
A 35-year-old P2002 woman presented with secondary amenorrhea for 8 months. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step in management?
A 25-year-old newly married woman presented to the Outpatient Clinic for routine gynecological examination. Which of the following has the highest diagnostic value?
A 34-year-old woman with a history of recurrent pregnancy loss was seen in the clinic. Which of the following is the best predictor for pregnancy complications?
A 40-year-old pregnant woman at 24 weeks of gestation with fever and did not seek any medical advice. What is the most likely reason for illness denial?
A 34-year-old woman came to the clinic with a history of primary infertility for 3 years. She was anxious, worried and depressed. Which of the following is a positive body language?

A 23-year-old nulligravida patient complains of inability to become pregnant after 3 months of trying. Patient periods are regular and normal. She had no prior reproductive problems. She currently is not on any contraception. Examination is normal. Her husband is 25-year-old healthy and has one autistic cousin and one with trisomy 21. Which of the following is the best action?

A 17-year-old woman comes at 39 weeks' gestation to the Emergency Department with no previous antenatal care. She delivered a healthy baby boy normally with no complications reported. Then she was given an injection of RhoGAM. What is the indication of RhoGAM?

options.text: Mother is Rh- and the baby is Rh+
Father is RH+ and the baby is Rh-
Mother is Rh+ and the baby is Rh-
Father is Rh- and the baby is Rh+

questions.stem: Which of the following tests is initially most appropriate?

A 67-year-old woman presented with vaginal itching and burning. Currently, she is only on calcium supplements. Physical examination revealed thinning and pallor of the vaginal mucosa and no discharge. Wet prep from the scant material present was negative for any organisms. Which of the following is the most appropriate initial treatment?
A 50-year-old woman presented with amenorrhea for the last 6 months and has unwanted hot flushes disturbing her night sleep. Which of the following serum levels would confirm the diagnosis?

A 28-year-old healthy woman presents to her gynecologist with history of inability to conceive after 2 years of trying. Menarche at 13-year-old, regular cycles every 36-40 days and 5-day periods. Not on any medications. Semenanalysis of husband showed normospermia, Cervical component examination is required. The basal body temperature showed a monophasic pattern. Which of the following is the most probable cause of the infertility?

A 26-year-old woman presented to the clinic with secondary amenorrhea of 6 months duration. She gave history of breast tenderness. On examination; bilateral breast whitish discharge from nipples. Her urine pregnancy test was negative and elevated serum prolactin levels. Which of the following radiological assessment is most appropriate?

A 14-year-old child presented to the clinic after being sexually abused 6 hours earlier. Genital examination confirmed anogenital erythema and mild bleeding vaginally, and labia majora was swollen and bruised. Blood pressure 120/70 mmHg, Heart rate 90 /min, Respiratory rate 20 /min Temperature 36.6° C, What is the most likely site of hymeneal tear that is suggestive of penile penetration?

A 27-year-old nulliparous is concerned about not having conceived after a year of regular, unprotected intercourse. The patient denied any major medical illnesses and takes no medications. The patient's spouse is reported to be healthy but has never fathered a child. What is the most appropriate initial step in evaluation after history and examination?

A 67-year-old woman a]ended the Gynecological Clinic for the follow up of lichen sclerosus diagnosed a few years earlier. Upon examination, a small mass measuring 0.5 x 0.5 cm was identified on her right labia majora. Punch biopsy was taken from the lesion and sent for histopathology. Which of the following is the most likely histopathological finding?
A 29-year-old woman is planning to become pregnant. She has a normal menstrual period every 30 days. Which of the following is the most appropriate to prescribe?

A 24-year-old newly married woman presents to the Emergency Room complaining of sudden sharp lower abdominal pain, she does not have regular menstrual cycles and does not remember when the her last menstrual cycle began, she is not known to have any previous medical illness and had no prior surgeries (see lab result). Blood pressure 100/70 mmH, Heart rate 76 /min Hb 11 130-170 g/L. (Male) 120-160 g/L (Female) Which of the following is the best advice?

options.text: Further tests including BhCG and ultrasound

questions.stem: A 35-year-old woman who is pregnant calls the clinic for an advice. She has just found out that her hCG level is elevated. Elevated hG level indicates which of the following?

options.text: A high level of hCG is indicative of an ectopic pregnancy
A high level of hCG in the second trimester is indicative of molar pregnancy
A high level of hCG can stimulate production of TRH, causing hyperthyroidism
A high level of hG in the second trimester is the most sensitive marker for Down syndrome

questions.stem: A 36-year-old woman Para 1 comes to the clinic for genetic counseling. Her first child was born with sickle cell disease. She has since remarried, and is requesting prenatal testing according to the premarital requirements in the country. Which of the following is appropriate to offer first?

A 30-year-old primigravida presents to the Emergency Room complaining of vaginal spotting for the last few days, her history reveals irregularity of the menstrual cycles and that she has been trying to conceive for the last 3 years. Abdominal examination reveals tenderness in the lower abdomen and the pelvic examination reveals a closed cervical Os with cervical motion tenderness (see lab results). Blood pressure 110/70 mmHg Heart rate 105 /min Temperature 36.6 °C Weight 60 kg Height 160 cm Hb 130 130-170 g/L (Male) 120-160 g/L (Female) HCT 038 0.42-0.52 (Male) 0.37-0.48 (Female) MCH 19 28-33 pg/cell MCHC 330 320-360 g/L. MCV 85 80-95 fl Platelets count 155 150-400 x 109/L WBC 4.6 4.5-10.5 x 109/L Which of the following is the most appropriate next step?

options.text: Perform an abdominal ultrasound of the pelvis
Know about the reason of infertility

questions.stem: Which of the following best describes the uterus in a normal pregnancy?

options.text: Palpable midway between the symphysis pubis and the umbilicus
Palpable just over the symphysis pubis
Palpable at the level of the umbilicus

questions.stem: A 32-year-old woman presents to the clinic with a 9-month history of amenorrhea concerning about her condition (see lab results). Thyroid-Stimulating Hormone 3 0.4 - 5.0 yU/mL Follicle-stimulating hormone 60 5-20 IU/L. (Follicular phase) 15-35 IU/L (Mid cycle peak) 5-15 IU/L (Luteal phase) 50-100 IU/L (Postmenopausal women) 5-20 IU/L (men) Testosterone 1 10.4-41.6 mol/L (Male) 0.7-2.8 nmol/L (Female) Luteinizing hormone 60 3-15 U/L (Male) 5-22 U/L (Follicular phase) 5-22 U/L (Luteal phase) 30-250 U/L (ovulatory phase) > 30 U/L (Postmenopausal) Prolactin 500 < 652 pmol/L. (Male) < 870 pmol/L (Female) Human chorionic gonadotropin 4 < 5 mlU/mL Which of the following is the most likely complication for this patient?

options.text: She is at significant risk of endometrial cancer
She is at increased risk for multiple gestation
She is at increased risk of ovarian cancer
She is at significant risk of osteoporosis

questions.stem: A 19-year-old woman presents to Labor and Delivery Ward in labor. She has not had any prenatal care. On examination, cervix is 4 cm dilated; the obstetrician palpate a bulging membrane but no fetal parts. Ultrasound demonstrates that the fetal head is in the fundus, the fetal spine is parallel to the mother's spine and the knees and hips are flexed. Both arms are flexed at the elbows. Which of the following is the best description of lie of this fetus?

A 36-year-old G3 P1011 woman is seen in preconception clinic for considering a pregnancy. She concerned of getting pregnant given the outcome of her first pregnancy. At 32 years of age, she delivered a term infant with Down syndrome. During that gestation, she had a second- trimester multiple marker screen been performed. Which of the following results would have been helpful?

options.text: Low hCG. low MSAFP, high estriol, high inhibin A
High hCG, low MSAFP, low estriol, high inhibin A
Low hCG, high MSAFP, high estriol, low inhibin A
Low hCG, high MSAFP, low estriol, low inhibin A

questions.stem: A 35-year-old pregnant woman at 34 weeks of gestation presented with labour pains. On physical examination, the cervix was 4 cm dilated. Cardiotocography was performed (see image), Blood pressure 135/88 mmHg Heart rate 89 /min Respiratory rate 18 /min Temperature 37.4° C Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 24-year-old woman has been applying a new herbal cream on her vulva for the last 2 weeks. She notices a burning sensation and itching along with redness at the area of application. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

options.text: Squamous intraepithelial lesions of the vulva

questions.stem: A 25-year-old woman complains of velvety, hyperpigmented plaques on her neck and axillae. She fails to conceive over the last 2 years despite regular intercourse. Her menses are irregular and occur once every 6 to 8 weeks. She started recently to experience increased facial hairs. What is the appropriate term of her skin hyperpigmentation?

A 22-year-old woman has multiple small cysts within the ovary, as well as excessive androgen production from the ovaries, anovulation, insulin resistance, hypertension, and hirsutism. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 24-year-old woman is complaining of failure to conceive over the last 16 months despite regular intercourse. She has infrequent menstruation occurring once every 6 to 8 weeks, with increased facial hair and acne. On ultrasound her ovaries had multiple small follicles each is 2.5 mm in diameter on the surface. Body mass index 37 kg/m2. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 24-year-old woman is complaining of failure to conceive over the last 16 months despite regular intercourse. She has infrequent menstruation occurring once every 6 to 8 weeks along with increased facial hair and acne. On ultrasound, her ovaries had multiple small follicles each is 2-5 mm diameter on the surface. She indicated that her main aim is getting pregnant. Body mass index 37 kg/m2 Which of the following is the initial step in management?

options.text: Weight reduction, metformin and clomiphene citrate
Weight reduction, in vitro fertilization and salicylic acid
Weight reduction, laparoscopic ovarian wedge resection and metformin

questions.stem: A 25-year-old woman complains of velvety, hyperpigmented plaques on her neck and under arm. She fails to conceive over the last 2 years despite regular intercourse. Her menses are infrequent and occurring once every 6 to 8 weeks. She notices recently increased facial hair. Her husband is healthy with a normal seminal analysis. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 26-year-old married woman presents to the Endocrinology-Gynecology clinic for a follow-up of her investigation results. Accordingly, a diagnosis of polycystic ovarian syndrome is made.
